origin.description: Computes the weighted sample mean of a numeric vector.
origin.usage:
weightedMean(x, w = NULL, idxs = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, refine = FALSE,
  ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A vector of weights the same length as x giving the weights to use for each element of x. Negative weights are treated as zero weights. Default value is equal weight to all values. If a missing-value weight exists, the result is always a missing value.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: refine
arguments.text: If TRUE and x is numeric, then extra effort is used to calculate the average with greater numerical precision, otherwise not.

origin.details: This function handles missing values consistently with weighted.mean. More precisely, if na.rm = FALSE, then any missing values in either x or w will give result NA_real_. If na.rm = TRUE, then all (x, w) data points for which x is missing are skipped. Note that if both x and w are missing for a data point, then it is also skipped (by the same rule). However, if only w is missing, then the final result will always be NA_real_ regardless of na.rm.
origin.value: Returns a numeric scalar. If x is of zero length, then NaN is returned, which is consistent with mean().
origin.example:
x <- 1:10
n <- length(x)

w <- rep(1, times = n)
m0 <- weighted.mean(x, w)
m1 <- weightedMean(x, w)
stopifnot(identical(m1, m0))

# Pull the mean towards zero
w[1] <- 5
m0 <- weighted.mean(x, w)
m1 <- weightedMean(x, w)
stopifnot(identical(m1, m0))

# Put even more weight on the zero
w[1] <- 8.5
m0 <- weighted.mean(x, w)
m1 <- weightedMean(x, w)
stopifnot(identical(m1, m0))

# All weight on the first value
w[1] <- Inf
m0 <- weighted.mean(x, w)
m1 <- weightedMean(x, w)
stopifnot(identical(m1, m0))

# All weight on the last value
w[1] <- 1
w[n] <- Inf
m0 <- weighted.mean(x, w)
m1 <- weightedMean(x, w)
stopifnot(identical(m1, m0))

# All weights set to zero
w <- rep(0, times = n)
m0 <- weighted.mean(x, w)
m1 <- weightedMean(x, w)
stopifnot(identical(m1, m0))

translation.description: Computes the weighted sample mean of a numeric vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric vector. This is x in R.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A vector of weights the same length as x. None gives every element equal weight. A weight of zero is skipped. The matrixStats manual says a negative weight counts as zero; matrixStats 1.5.0 keeps it in the sum, and this function does too. A missing weight makes the result missing when the paired x value is present.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based vector indicating the subset of elements to operate over. None means no subsetting. Integer, numeric, and logical subscripts follow the matrixStats index rules, including negative exclusion and logical recycling.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, points whose x is missing are skipped. This is na.rm in R.

arguments.name: refine
arguments.text: If True, a second pass adds the weighted residuals of the first average. The default is False.

translation.details: Missing values follow matrixStats::weightedMean. If na_rm is False, a missing value in x or in w makes the result NaN, except that a weight of zero skips that point before x is read. If na_rm is True, points whose x is missing are skipped, including a point where both x and w are missing. A missing weight paired with a present x still makes the result NaN. The sum and the residual pass run in the Rust crate weightedmean.
translation.value: A numeric scalar. If x is empty, or the selected points have total weight zero, the result is NaN.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.weightedmean import weightedMean

x = np.arange(1, 11, dtype=float)
w = np.ones(x.size)
m1 = weightedMean(x, w)

w = w.copy()
w[0] = 5
m1 = weightedMean(x, w)

w[0] = 8.5
m1 = weightedMean(x, w)

w[0] = np.inf
m1 = weightedMean(x, w)

w[0] = 1
w[-1] = np.inf
m1 = weightedMean(x, w)

w = np.zeros(x.size)
m1 = weightedMean(x, w)
